result.title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
result.summary: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall frontier on ambiguous text-to-SQL (Ambrosia), and on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), it raises diversity at about the same pass@$K$.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PoolDPP：用行列式点过程刻画语言模型输出的质量与多样性，并通过从可处理提议分布抽取候选池、重要性加权及贪心 MAP 变体近似实现 K-DPP 采样，给出池大小 O(1/N) 的 KL 收敛界，并在开放生成、歧义 text-to-SQL 和 GSM8K 上验证多样性与质量权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其基于嵌入几何刻画差异、并用候选集筛选近似难解目标分布的思路，可能为 latent 假设的多样化采样与视觉证据候选筛选提供参考，可供核查。
